claim: For the Kapitaniak–Mohammadi–Mekhilef hidden-attractor flow \(\dot x=z\), \(\dot y=-x-z\), \(\dot z=\tfrac{1}{10}x+5y-z+xy-\tfrac{3}{10}xz+a\), every compactly supported invariant probability measure \(\mu\) satisfies, with \(q=\int x^2\,d\mu\), \(\int x\,d\mu=\int z\,d\mu=\int xz\,d\mu=0\), \(\int xy\,d\mu=-q\), \(\int yz\,d\mu=q\), and the exact stationary height law \(\int y\,d\mu=-a/5+q/5\). Moreover \(\operatorname{Var}_\mu(y)\ge q\), with equality if and only if \(\mu\) is the equilibrium point mass at \(E_a=(0,-a/5,0)\). Hence every non-equilibrium compact stationary state has \(\int y\,d\mu>-a/5\), \(\operatorname{Var}_\mu(y)>\int x^2\,d\mu=5(\int y\,d\mu+a/5)\), and positive mass in the half-space \(y>-a/5\); every nonconstant periodic orbit obeys the corresponding time-average identities.
integrity: The Lie-derivative identities are exact polynomial identities and were replayed by a packaged exact-arithmetic checker. The primary open-access full text was inspected for the system equation, equilibrium, numerical dynamics, and scope. No independent audit or external validation is claimed.
limitations: The theorem concerns compactly supported invariant probability measures of the exact ODE. It does not prove existence of the source's numerically displayed chaotic attractor, identify a physical measure, or determine basin geometry or bifurcation thresholds. The originality search was targeted and cannot exclude unindexed equivalent work.
title: A polynomial coboundary and stationary height gap in a hidden-attractor flow
